For the purpose of determining register group overlap constraints, mask elements have EEW=1.

 _The overlap constraints are designed to support resumable exceptions in machineswithout register renaming._

Any instruction encoding that violates the overlap constraints is reserved.

When source and destination registers overlap and have different EEW, the instruction is mask- and tail-agnostic, regardless of the setting of the `vta` and `vma` bits in `vtype` .</previous>
<target>The largest vector register group used by an instruction can not be greater than 8 vector registers (i.e., EMUL≤8), and if a vector instruction would require greater than 8 vector registers in a group, the instruction encoding is reserved. For example, a widening operation that produces a widened vector register group result when LMUL=8 is reserved as this would imply a result EMUL=16.

Widened scalar values, e.g., input and output to a widening reduction operation, are held in the first element of a vector register and have EMUL=1.</target>
